stories.headline: Intel posts fastest revenue growth since 2011 as data-center CPU demand outruns supply

key_facts.fact: Intel reported second-quarter 2026 revenue of $16.1 billion, up 25% year over year, its strongest quarterly revenue growth in more than fifteen years.
key_facts.excerpt: Second-quarter revenue was $16.1 billion, up 25% year-over-year (YoY). ... 'Our Q2 results represent our strongest revenue growth in more than fifteen years,' said Lip-Bu Tan, Intel CEO.

key_facts.fact: The Data Center and AI unit drove the quarter with $6.3 billion in revenue, up 59%, while client computing rose 13% to $8.9 billion and Intel Foundry rose 31% to $5.8 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Client Computing and Physical AI Group (CCPG) $8.9 billion up 13% | Data Center and AI (DCAI) 6.3 billion up 59% | Intel Foundry 5.8 billion up 31%

key_facts.fact: Results beat Wall Street estimates of $14.42 billion in revenue and 21 cents of adjusted EPS; Intel posted adjusted EPS of 42 cents.
key_facts.excerpt: Wall Street had penciled in revenue of $14.42 billion and adjusted earnings of 21 cents per share... Intel posted adjusted EPS of 42 cents.

key_facts.fact: On a GAAP basis Intel reported an $11 billion net loss, or $2.16 per share, driven by a $12.5 billion mark-to-market loss on escrowed shares tied to its CHIPS Act agreement with the US government.
key_facts.excerpt: On a GAAP basis, the company reported a net loss of $11 billion, or $2.16 per share, driven by a $12.5 billion mark-to-market loss on escrowed shares tied to its CHIPS Act agreement with the U.S. government.

key_facts.fact: Intel said its data-center operations cannot keep up with orders and has signed 10 long-term contracts with server CPU buyers, structured around fixed pricing commitments or guaranteed purchase volumes.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel said its data center operations cannot keep up with orders, leaving the company unable to fully meet customer demand. The company has signed 10 long-term contracts with server CPU buyers, structured around either fixed pricing commitments or guaranteed purchase volumes.

key_facts.fact: Intel guided third-quarter revenue to $15.8-$16.8 billion versus analyst estimates of $15.1 billion, and CFO David Zinsner said 2026 capital spending was raised from $18 billion to $20 billion, with spending 'up meaningfully next year'; the stock rose about 5% after hours.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel expects third-quarter revenue between $15.8 billion and $16.8 billion, compared with analysts' average estimate of $15.1 billion... booming demand has prompted Intel to raise its capital expenditure forecast for this year from $18 billion to $20 billion, with spending expected to be 'up meaningfully next year' as well... pushing its shares up 5.2% in after-hours trade

key_facts.fact: Data Center and AI operating income grew from $600 million a year earlier to $2.5 billion, while the foundry business still lost about $2.1 billion in the quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel's Data Center and AI division, which saw revenue rise 59% to $6.3 billion and operating income grow from $600 million to $2.5 billion... the foundry business, which lost $2.1 billion

stories.headline: Nvidia commits $1.5B prepayment to Amkor to expand US advanced chip packaging

key_facts.fact: Amkor Technology announced on July 23 a multi-year strategic partnership with Nvidia to develop advanced semiconductor packaging and test technologies, with Nvidia providing a prepayment to expand Amkor's US advanced packaging capacity.
key_facts.excerpt: $1.5 Billion Multi-Year Advanced Packaging and Development Agreement to Support Expansion of Amkor's U.S. Advanced Packaging Capacity ... Under the agreement, NVIDIA will provide a prepayment to support the expansion of Amkor's U.S. advanced packaging capacity.

key_facts.fact: The deal is worth $1.5 billion and the companies will jointly develop packaging and testing focused on combining different types of chips in a single package for Nvidia's AI and accelerated-computing platforms.
key_facts.excerpt: Amkor Technology said on Thursday it had entered a multi-year agreement with Nvidia worth $1.5 billion to expand advanced semiconductor packaging and test capacity in the U.S. ... focusing on combining different types of chips in a single package.

key_facts.fact: The money funds Amkor's Arizona expansion, where it is building a $2 billion packaging and test plant in Peoria that was awarded $407 million under the CHIPS and Science Act; the structure is a prepayment against future capacity, not an equity stake.
key_facts.excerpt: the money will fund the expansion of Amkor's operations in Arizona, where the company is already building a $2 billion packaging and test facility in Peoria... The prepayment is not an equity stake. It is cash committed upfront against future capacity... Amkor's Peoria plant was awarded $407 million under the CHIPS and Science Act

key_facts.fact: Amkor shares rose roughly 12% in after-hours trading on the announcement.
key_facts.excerpt: The agreement, announced on 23 July, pushed Amkor shares up by roughly 12% in after-hours trading.

key_facts.fact: Amkor already packages chips for both Nvidia and AMD and in June signed a 10-year advanced-packaging partnership with TSMC in the United States.
key_facts.excerpt: In June, Amkor entered a 10-year partnership with TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, to enhance semiconductor packaging capabilities in the United States... Amkor is also working with Advanced Micro Devices to package the semiconductor company's chips.

key_facts.fact: Neither company disclosed a timeline or how much new capacity the $1.5 billion buys.
key_facts.excerpt: Neither company disclosed a timeline, or how much fresh capacity $1.5 billion actually buys.

stories.headline: AMD unveils Zen 6 'Venice' server chips and ties its Helios racks to rival Cerebras wafers

key_facts.fact: At its Advancing AI 2026 event on July 23, AMD announced the 6th Gen EPYC 9006 'Venice' server processors on the Zen 6 architecture, with up to 96 Zen 6 cores/192 threads or up to 256 Zen 6c cores/512 threads per socket.
key_facts.excerpt: AMD today announced the 6th Gen EPYC 'Venice' server processors powered by the 'Zen 6' CPU microarchitecture... CPU core counts of up to 96-core/192-thread on chips with 'Zen 6' cores, and up to 256-core/512-thread on chips with compacted 'Zen 6c' cores.

key_facts.fact: The Venice family is in production now, with EPYC 9006 SP7 shipping in Q4 2026, SP8 in H1 2027, and the Venice-X and LP variants in H2 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: AMD EPYC 'Venice' series is in production now, with the 9006 SP7 series shipping in Q4 2026, 9006 SP8 bound for the first half of 2027, the 9006X SP7 series HPC processors bound for the second half of 2027, along with the 9006 LP series.

key_facts.fact: The high-end Venice-X (EPYC 9006X) pairs 96 Zen 6 cores with 1,152 MB of stacked 3D V-Cache and boost clocks up to 5.15 GHz, on a 16-channel memory subsystem supporting DDR5-8000 RDIMMs or MRDIMMs at 12,800 MT/s for up to 1.6 TB/s of bandwidth.
key_facts.excerpt: It supports 16-channel memory, either with standard DDR5 RDIMMs at up to 8,000 MT/s or with new MRDIMMs 12,800 MT/s, offering up to 1.6 TB/s of aggregate memory bandwidth... AMD says clocks are much higher here, claiming Venice-X tops out at 5.15 GHz

key_facts.fact: Also at Advancing AI, AMD and Cerebras Systems announced a technical partnership combining AMD Helios rack-scale systems with the Cerebras Wafer-Scale Engine in a disaggregated inference workflow expected to deliver up to 5x higher tokens per second per watt.
key_facts.excerpt: AMD (NASDAQ: AMD) and Cerebras Systems (NASDAQ: CBRS) announced a technical partnership to deliver a new disaggregated AI inference solution that combines AMD Helios rackscale solutions with the Cerebras Wafer-Scale Engine... expected to deliver up to 5x higher tokens per second per watt (T/s/W)

key_facts.fact: AMD Helios handles prompt processing and long context windows while the Cerebras Wafer-Scale Engine handles memory-bandwidth-intensive token generation; Cerebras will deploy Helios systems in its own data centers and the joint solution arrives first on Cerebras Cloud in the second half of 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: AMD Helios provides ultra-high throughput, processing prompts and large context windows. The Cerebras Wafer-Scale Engine accelerates the memory-bandwidth-intensive token generation, with ultra-low latency... Cerebras plans to deploy AMD Helios systems in its data centers, with the joint solution expected to become available initially through Cerebras Cloud in the second half of 2026.

key_facts.fact: The Cerebras deal, announced on stage during CEO Lisa Su's keynote, closes a gap in AMD's portfolio that Nvidia filled by paying $20 billion to acquihire Groq in December; Cerebras' wafer-scale engines use on-chip SRAM rather than HBM4 memory.
key_facts.excerpt: The collaboration, announced on stage during AMD CEO Lisa Su's Advancing AI keynote Thursday, closes a gap in AMD's portfolio that cost Nvidia $20 billion to acquihire from Groq back in December... unlike GPUs, Cerebras' wafer scale engines (WSE) don't rely on HBM4 but instead use on-chip SRAM that's orders of magnitude faster.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft plans to deploy Venice-X in Azure HXv2 instances next year, and AMD says the broader Venice family uses TSMC 2nm compute dies.
key_facts.excerpt: AMD confirmed Venice SP7 is already in production and said the broader Venice family will include higher-core parts built on TSMC's 2nm compute dies and multi-die IO designs... Microsoft reportedly plans to deploy Venice-X in Azure HXv2 instances next year.

stories.headline: AMD partners with Eric Trump-backed Foundation to power Phantom humanoid robots

key_facts.fact: Foundation Future Industries said on July 23 it is partnering with AMD to co-develop autonomous humanoid robots for military and industrial use, using AMD Ryzen AI Embedded X100 Series processors to build the second version of its robot, Phantom MK-2; deal value was not disclosed.
key_facts.excerpt: Eric Trump-backed Foundation Future Industries said on Thursday it is partnering with AMD to use its chips to co-develop autonomous humanoid robots for military and industrial use... Foundation plans to use AMD Ryzen AI Embedded X100 Series processors — introduced by the chipmaker in January this year — to build the second version of its robot, Phantom MK-2.

key_facts.fact: Eric Trump, son of US President Donald Trump, has been an investor in the startup since early this year and serves as chief strategy advisor.
key_facts.excerpt: The son of U.S. President Donald Trump has been an investor in the start-up since early this year and serves as chief strategy advisor, the company said.

key_facts.fact: Foundation, founded in 2024, says its Phantom MK-1 robots helped build more than 24,000 cars in 2025; it will open a factory in October capable of building 5,000 robots a year and start another early next year with capacity for 50,000.
key_facts.excerpt: The start-up, founded in 2024, said it has deployed its Phantom MK-1 robots to contribute in building more than 24,000 cars in 2025. In October, the company will open a factory capable of building 5,000 Phantom robots annually, with plans to start building another facility early next year with an annual capacity of 50,000 robots, CEO Sankaet Pathak told Reuters.

key_facts.fact: Industrial robots are leased at about $100,000 per year, while defense units for materials handling and reconnaissance are sold to the government at $300,000 each.
key_facts.excerpt: Each industrial-use robots, leased to customers, cost about $100,000 per year, Pathak said. On the defense side, the company is developing robots for materials handling and reconnaissance, which are sold to the government at $300,000 a unit.

key_facts.fact: The architecture uses AMD Kria AI system-on-modules with X100 processors as the robot's embedded 'brain', plus AMD FPGA-based systems for Phantom's hands, sensing and real-time control.
key_facts.excerpt: The companies are developing an embedded computing architecture for Foundation's production robots using AMD Kria AI system-on-modules powered by AMD Ryzen AI Embedded X100 Series processors... The collaboration covers the development of an X100 Series-powered embedded 'brain' for the robot, along with AMD FPGA-based systems supporting Phantom's hands, sensing and real-time control.

key_facts.fact: AMD launched a full-stack robotics push the same day — the Ryzen AI Embedded X100 series plus a Kria AI system-on-module, a Robotics Development Kit and the open-source Robotics Sophie Suite — claiming it can outperform Nvidia's Orin and Thor on system-level robotics workloads; Foundation is migrating from Intel and Nvidia to AMD.
key_facts.excerpt: AMD today promised deterministic real-time control, unified CPU–GPU–NPU memory, and an open, non–vendor-locked software stack that it claimed can outperform NVIDIA Orin and Thor on system-level robotics workloads... humanoid robot developer Foundation Robotics, which is migrating from Intel and NVIDIA to AMD X100 and future FPGA-based hand control.

key_facts.fact: Foundation's Phantom machines have been tested in Ukraine and the company has won Pentagon contracts to develop humanoid robots for the US military.
key_facts.excerpt: Its Phantom machines have been tested in Ukraine, and Foundation has since won Pentagon contracts to develop humanoid robots for the US military.

stories.headline: Chinese GPU maker MetaX confidentially files for a Hong Kong IPO targeted by year-end

key_facts.fact: MetaX, a Shanghai-based GPU designer, has confidentially filed for a Hong Kong listing and is targeting an IPO by the end of 2026, working with Huatai International Financial Holdings on the share sale.
key_facts.excerpt: MetaX, a Chinese maker of graphics processing units (GPUs), has confidentially filed for a listing in Hong Kong... The Shanghai-based company was targeting an initial public offering (IPO) by the end of this year... MetaX was working with Huatai International Financial Holdings on the potential share sale.

key_facts.fact: The filing surfaced hours after Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing said it would let every listing applicant keep its application confidential, part of the bourse's biggest set of listing reforms since 2018.
key_facts.excerpt: The filing surfaced hours after Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing said it would let every listing applicant keep its application confidential, part of the bourse's biggest set of listing reforms since 2018.

key_facts.fact: MetaX's board cleared the path in June 2026 with a plan to issue H shares equal to no more than 5% of enlarged capital, with proceeds earmarked for next-generation GPU development, software ecosystem, supply-chain investments and possible acquisitions.
key_facts.excerpt: In June 2026, the company said in a filing that it planned to issue H shares — stock listed in Hong Kong — equal to no more than 5% of its enlarged capital, with proceeds earmarked for next-generation GPU development, its software ecosystem, supply-chain investments and potential acquisitions. Shareholders approved the plan at a meeting later that month.

key_facts.fact: The IPO plan comes amid a capital-raising surge by Chinese AI chipmakers, with peers Biren Technology, Iluvatar CoreX and Moore Threads listing in Shanghai or Hong Kong since late 2025, driven by Beijing's semiconductor self-reliance push under US export controls.
key_facts.excerpt: The IPO plan comes amid a surge of capital-raising by China's artificial intelligence chipmakers, with peers Biren Technology, Iluvatar CoreX and Moore Threads listing in Shanghai or Hong Kong since late 2025. The wave has been driven by Beijing's semiconductor self-reliance initiative amid US export controls.

key_facts.fact: MetaX began trading in Shanghai in December after raising $586 million and its shares have climbed 564% since, lifting market value to 278 billion yuan ($41 billion); the company was founded in 2020 by former AMD engineers.
key_facts.excerpt: The maker of graphics processing units for artificial intelligence developers started trading in Shanghai in December after raising $586 million. It has soared 564% since the IPO, lifting its market value to 278 billion yuan ($41 billion).

key_facts.fact: MetaX was founded in September 2020 by former AMD engineers Chen Weiliang, Peng Li and Yang Jian, and has drawn investor interest as Beijing pushes domestic alternatives to Nvidia's AI chips.
key_facts.excerpt: Founded in 2020, MetaX has emerged as one of China's most closely watched GPU start-ups. The company has attracted investor interest in part because its founding team includes former AMD executives, as Beijing pushes to develop domestic alternatives to Nvidia's AI chips amid tightening US export restrictions.

stories.headline: Robotics startup Genesis AI in talks for a $500M round at a $3B pre-money valuation

key_facts.fact: Genesis AI, which builds foundation models meant to run inside a wide range of robots, is in talks to raise about $500 million at a pre-money valuation of roughly $3 billion, according to Bloomberg.
key_facts.excerpt: Genesis AI, the startup building foundation models that it hopes will run inside a wide range of robots, is in talks to raise about $500m, according to Bloomberg. A round of that size would value the company at roughly $3bn... The $3bn figure is described as a pre-money valuation.

key_facts.fact: Premji Invest is said to be in discussions to lead the round, with HSG (formerly Sequoia China) and Northzone weighing further investment; the deal is not final and terms could shift.
key_facts.excerpt: Premji Invest is said to be in discussions to lead the round, with HSG, formerly Sequoia China, and Northzone weighing further investment... None of the firms has commented, and the line-up could still shift.

key_facts.fact: Genesis emerged from stealth in July 2025 with a $105 million seed round co-led by Eclipse Ventures and Khosla Ventures, so a $500 million follow-on inside 12 months would be a steep markup.
key_facts.excerpt: Genesis emerged from stealth in July 2025 with a $105m seed round co-led by Eclipse Ventures and Khosla Ventures, among the larger seeds of that year. A $500m follow-on inside 12 months would mark a steep markup.

key_facts.fact: The company was founded by Zhou Xian, a Carnegie Mellon robotics PhD, and Théophile Gervet, a former Mistral research scientist, with backers including Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel and Bpifrance; it unveiled its GENE-26.5 foundation model in May 2026 and its Eno robot in June.
key_facts.excerpt: Genesis was founded by Zhou Xian, a Carnegie Mellon robotics PhD, and Théophile Gervet, a former Mistral research scientist... with Bpifrance, HSG, Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, Daniela Rus and Vladlen Koltun also among the backers... which unveiled its GENE-26.5 foundation model in May 2026 and launched its own robot Eno in June

key_facts.fact: Genesis pitches GENE-26.5 as a universal model across robot form factors, backed by an in-house physics engine that generates synthetic data hundreds of thousands of times faster than real time and a $300 sensor glove for capturing human motion.
key_facts.excerpt: The company's pitch is built around GENE-26.5, a universal model designed to work across different robot form factors. That includes the Eno wheeled robot, dexterous hands, an in-house physics engine that can generate synthetic data hundreds of thousands of times faster than real time, and a $300 sensor glove for capturing human motion.

stories.headline: Trump expands data-center power pledge to 200+ utilities, developers and governors

key_facts.fact: President Trump announced on July 23 at EPA headquarters an expansion of the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, bringing more than 200 additional utilities, data-center developers, cooperatives and states into the commitment.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, President Donald J. Trump heralded a historic expansion of the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, bringing more than 200 additional utilities, data center developers, cooperatives, and states into this growing national commitment.

key_facts.fact: The White House says the pledge now covers roughly 80% of all power delivered to US homes and businesses and protects 263 million Americans when a data center is built nearby.
key_facts.excerpt: Together they cover roughly 80% of the power delivered to American homes and businesses, protecting 263 million Americans — three-quarters of the country — when a data center is built nearby.

key_facts.fact: The White House counts more than 150 utilities and cooperatives and 28 data-center developers among signatories, alongside the 7 largest US hyperscalers and AI companies that signed in March.
key_facts.excerpt: 150+ Utilities and cooperatives — from generation-and-transmission co-ops to municipal utilities and state associations... 28 Firms that build and operate the physical facilities driving new load... 7 The largest U.S. hyperscalers and AI companies, committed since the March round of the pledge.

key_facts.fact: The pledge, first announced in Trump's February 24, 2026 State of the Union and signed on March 4 by Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Oracle and xAI, commits signatories to build, bring or buy new power supply, pay for delivery-infrastructure upgrades, and pay negotiated rates whether or not they use the electricity.
key_facts.excerpt: President Trump first announced the Ratepayer Protection Pledge in his State of the Union address on February 24, 2026. On March 4, 2026, seven leading AI companies and hyperscalers — Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Oracle, and xAI — signed the Ratepayer Protection Pledge at the White House... The Pledge commits signatories to five obligations: building, bringing, or buying new power supply; paying for all new power delivery infrastructure upgrades; paying negotiated rates whether or not they use the electricity...

key_facts.fact: AP reported the pledge has been signed by 23 governors and at least 187 companies, and noted the pledge is voluntary and nonbinding while Trump promised electricity prices would fall as a result.
key_facts.excerpt: The White House said Thursday the pledge has been signed by 23 governors and at least 187 companies... The president promised that electricity prices would drop because of the nonbinding pledge, saying there would be a surplus of power.

key_facts.fact: New signatories include Republican governors Jeff Landry (Louisiana), Brian Kemp (Georgia), Jim Pillen (Nebraska) and Brad Little (Idaho), plus utilities Duke Energy and NextEra Energy; the event was held with Energy Secretary Chris Wright and EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin.
key_facts.excerpt: Republican governors signed on to the agreement, including Louisiana's Jeff Landry, Georgia's Brian Kemp, Nebraska's Jim Pillen, and Idaho's Brad Little... The other new signatures added to the pledge include major utilities, such as Duke Energy and NextEra Energy.

key_facts.fact: House lawmakers this week advanced the bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act out of committee, which would require state regulators to set standards making data centers and hyperscalers that use over 100 megawatts cover the cost of new generation, transmission and infrastructure upgrades.
key_facts.excerpt: House lawmakers earlier this week advanced the bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act out of committee, which would require state regulators to create standards for new data centers and hyperscalers that consume over 100 megawatts of electricity to cover the costs of new generation, transmission, and infrastructure upgrades.
